content: Nuclear protein localization protein 4 homolog, commonly referred to as NPLOC4, is a protein encoded by the NPLOC4 gene in humans. To investigate the function of NPLOC4, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line, named Nploc4tm1a(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was developed as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at creating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers worldwide. The mouse line was generated at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a comprehensive and standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the consequences of NPLOC4 gene deletion. A total of 26 different tests were conducted, and two phenotypes were identified. Notably, no homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, indicating that these embryos did not survive to the weaning stage. The remaining tests were performed on adult mice that were heterozygous for the mutation. In these heterozygous mutant mice, no significant abnormalities were observed. Additionally, NPLOC4 has been demonstrated to interact with the protein UFD1L.
